evidence:
Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=ecea6eb5d02c
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - none
MINOR:
  - `review_select.py` delta: `norm.replace("_", "")` is unbounded string mangling instead of an explicit status alias map; `won_tfix`→`wontfix`-style collisions can silently widen the closed set, weakening the "closed status comes from the authoritative backlog" invariant (design contract, `is_closed` hunk).
  - The new `test_mixed_case_closed_status` passes via the raw-lower branch if `CLOSED_STATUSES` already contains `wont_fix`, so the added `replace("_","")` path may have zero coverage; add a case only reachable through normalization to prove which branch decides closure.
  - Prior finding disposition=ACTIONED is not fully substantiated: no delta test asserts the printed `mtime_fallback=` line end-to-end with populated `meta` (the new tests cover `skipped_closed`/`item=` and `is_closed` only), so the observability half of AC-3 for the mtime path remains untested.
  - `test_item_closed_skip_output` stubs `backlog.get_epic`, so it verifies skip plumbing/output shape but not that a real authoritative closed status reaches `is_closed`; combined with the underscore change, the authority→skip wiring is only indirectly covered.
NIT:
  - `test_item_closed_skip_output` asserts loose substrings (`skipped_closed=1`, `item=BI-PF-7`) without pinning `status=ok` on the same line, so a regression that reports skip but still fails the item would pass the test.
SUMMARY:
  - Delta correctly resolves the pending greppability NIT (`item=<id>`) and adds closed-skip/mixed-case tests; no blockers and no AC regression in the delta.
  - Top risks: the underscore-normalization in `is_closed` is an implicit, possibly untested widening of the closed set, and one prior disposition (printed `mtime_fallback` observability) is marked ACTIONED without covering evidence.
  - Recommend explicit status aliasing plus one end-to-end assertion of the printed fallback marker before merge.
RECOMMENDATION: no hard blocker (MAJOR/MINOR/NIT advisory; HIL decides)

applicability.reason: Single selector helper plus two callers.

BLOCKER: AC-2 requires regression tests covering both callers, but declared affected_files only include test-framework/tests/test_fix_guard.py — no test file covers architect_review.py's use of the shared helper, so the AC cannot be met as scoped.
MAJOR: Closed-item status source and trust boundary are unspecified: if status comes from a PR-modifiable backlog file, the skip becomes a gate bypass — AC-3 demands explicit, non-bypassable enforcement; design must pin the authoritative status source and state tamper handling.

AC-3 covers mtime fallback observability (REVIEW_ORDER_MTIME_FALLBACK), but test_matrix/test_matrix entries only test recorded-at ordering and closed-skip; no fail-able test asserts fallback emission, so the observability contract is unverified.

"Print skipped count/fallback" (stdout text) is the sole observability with runbook N/A; without structured output, exit-code semantics, or a machine-checkable marker, skipped-vs-failed cannot be distinguished reliably by CI — weakens AC-3 verifiability.
MINOR: FR-1 edge case "Z vs +00:00 timestamps" is not reflected in invariants or any listed test; timezone-normalization ordering invariant should be stated and tested to preserve determinism across contributors/CI.
Failure matrix cases (malformed review skipped, REVIEW_ORDER_DETERMINISTIC) have no corresponding tests in the proof/test plan.
Rollback ("Revert the change"/"Revert PR") lacks a stated verification step (e.g., post-revert gate run) though risk is low for CI-only tooling.
Guardrail checklist answers are not embedded in the design artifact (reversibility, blast radius/dry-run, invariants) — required by CL-008 to pre-empt review corrections.
NIT: risks and out_of_scope are "Not specified" in the gate context; a one-line risk note (e.g., legacy reviews without `at`) would align with the spec pack.
Design should record the language-rule classification (scripts/dev = tooling Python) explicitly to preempt a Gate 1.5 language finding for review_select.py.
SUMMARY: Design direction is sound: single shared selector, recorded-at-first ordering, explicit closed-skip reporting match the ACs and guardrails.

Top risks: missing architect-review regression test (AC-2 unmet within declared files), unspecified closed-status trust boundary enabling gate bypass, and untested/soft observability for mtime fallback and skip counts.

MAJOR: Delta `risks` ("A PR could alter backlog status") and delta `security` ("never a PR-local ad-hoc flag") state contradictory tamper models for the same closed-status field, leaving AC-3's non-bypass guarantee ambiguous within this delta.

`security`/`risks` depend on a "close guard" and "independent verification" that appear in no `dependencies` or `affected_files` row; the anti-bypass control for AC-3 is asserted but undeclared in the changed scope.
MINOR: `ac_evidence` for AC-2/AC-3 cites implementation files (`review_select.py`, `fix_guard.py`) while `test_matrix` cites tests for the same ACs; evidence types disagree inside one delta.

`coverage[FR-1]` lists only `test_latest_review_uses_recorded_at_not_mtime`, but `test_matrix` AC-1 also lists `test_selector_normalizes_timestamps_and_skips_malformed` — coverage and test_matrix are out of sync.

Guardrail "No silent skip" conflicts with `runtime_contract.failure_behavior` ("malformed reviews skipped"): no emitted signal is specified, and a silently dropped malformed newest review can change selection outcome.
`design_pack.security` asserts a "backlog store/API" source while `runtime_contract.adapter` remains filesystem-only; the closed-status source is not anchored to any declared component.
NIT: `functional_spec.observability` ("Print skipped count/fallback") and `design_pack.observability` ("status=ok skipped_closed=<n>") phrase the emitted contract differently; single-source the marker format.
Delta `risks` row 2 restates concerns already carried by the `security` row; merge into one authoritative statement to prevent future drift.
SUMMARY: Delta adds useful guardrails (language rule, rollback verification, explicit skip marker) but introduces an internal trust-model contradiction between `risks` and `security` and leaves evidence/coverage rows cross-mismatched.
Top risks: AC-3 non-bypass claim rests on undeclared controls, and ac_evidence/coverage rows do not line up with test_matrix, weakening traceability for AC-1/AC-2.
Resolve the risks-vs-security contradiction and align evidence rows with tests before Gate 1.5/1 approval.

MAJOR: Delta introduces control dependencies (`core/backlog.py`, `scripts/dev/gate2_completion_check.py`) but leaves `contracts.files`/`affected_files` unchanged, so the AC-3 anti-bypass control has no declared file/evidence row in the same delta (guardrail: matching rows must update together).
MINOR: `coverage` has no row for AC-2's tests (`test_shared_selector_used_for_reviews`, `test_architect_review_uses_shared_selector`) that `test_matrix` lists — coverage/test_matrix diverge on a new AC.
`functional_spec.traceability`/`requirements` contain only FR-1/FR-2; AC-2 (shared deterministic helper with tests covering both callers) maps to no requirement or traceability row.
Delta `observability` rows emit only `skipped_closed=<n>`; no emitted signal is specified for the mtime fallback, which AC-3 requires to be explicit and observable.
`functional_spec.dependencies` (only `BI-PF-1243`) is not synced with the expanded `design_pack.dependencies` in the same delta.
NIT: AC-2 architect-review tests are named and placed in `test_fix_guard.py` with no architect-review test file declared in `contracts.files`.
`functional_spec.data_lifecycle` states "No runtime data" while the selector reads on-disk review evidence files.
SUMMARY: Delta resolves several prior findings (contradicting `risks` tamper row removed, observability wording unified, `adapter` now names `core/backlog.py`, AC-1 coverage row synced).
Verdict: sound design direction; top residual risks are the undeclared file rows for the close-guard control dependency and incomplete AC-2 traceability/coverage.

BLOCKER: AC-3 unmet: `review_select.latest_review` applies the mtime tie-break/fallback silently — no log, counter, or marker when `at` is missing/degraded; design failure_matrix `REVIEW_ORDER_MTIME_FALLBACK` ("log/record degraded ordering") is not implemented.

mtime fallback is a silent gate-ordering path: a legacy review with no `at` can win selection with zero runtime evidence that degraded ordering was used (test coverage does not make it observable in CI output).
MAJOR: `fix_guard.problems` now returns `[]` before the `fix_impact missing` check whenever the selected review has no BLOCKER/MAJOR findings (or no review is found) — silently drops existing enforcement; behavior change not authorized by the approved contract ("No change to review findings or dispositions").
`status=ok` is printed unconditionally in the `--all` branch before `bad` is evaluated, so a failing gate still emits `status=ok` — misleading observability that undermines AC-3.

`CLOSED_STATUSES` is hardcoded in `review_select.py` instead of reusing the `core/backlog.py` status authority named in design dependencies; vocabulary drift risks wrongly enforcing (or skipping) items as backlog statuses evolve.

Design claims `test_selector_normalizes_timestamps_and_skips_malformed` covers the mtime fallback, but every fixture includes `at` — the legacy missing-`at` path is never exercised (FR-1 data_rules "mtime is fallback only" untested).
MINOR: Closed-item skip in `--item` mode is silent (no `skipped_closed` output); AC-3 observability only satisfied for `--all`.
`problems()` computes the identical `required`/`req` list twice — dead duplicated block left in the gate path.
No test asserts the `skipped_closed=<n>` output or count (FR-2 "Skipped count" acceptance), only `enforced()` returns False.
NIT: `return found or None` is redundant (`latest_review` already returns `{}`/dict).
Function-local `from review_select import ...` in `architect_review._latest_review` runs on every call; module-level import matches the `fix_guard` pattern.
SUMMARY: Shared selector and closed-skip are directionally right, but AC-3 is not satisfied: mtime fallback is silent at runtime and its claimed test coverage does not exist.
Two gate-semantics/observability defects in `fix_guard` (early return bypassing `fix_impact missing`; unconditional `status=ok`) weaken CI enforcement credibility.
Top risks: unauthorized enforcement change, misleading gate output, and duplicated closed-status vocabulary drifting from the backlog authority.

MAJOR: `is_closed` now delegates to `backlog.section({"status": ...}) == "done"` (review_select.py delta); equivalence to the prior CLOSED_STATUSES set is unproven and untested — if section() maps only literal "done", previously-closed statuses stop being skipped and get enforced (AC-1 regression); if it maps broadly, open items could be silently skipped (gate bypass).

No delta test exercises the changed `is_closed` authority path or asserts the new fix-guard `mtime_fallback=<n>` output; the only added test covers `review_select.latest_review` meta, so the closed-skip semantics change ships without a fail-able test (design guardrail: no silent behaviour change without a test).
MINOR: `--all` invokes `latest_review` twice per item (once discarded, solely to populate `meta`) instead of threading `meta` through `problems()`; duplicated file reads and the counter could diverge from the selection actually enforced.

mtime-fallback observability exists only on `--all` and in architect_review; the fix-guard `--item`/single-item path remains silent, extending the prior pending `--item` observability gap to AC-3 fallback.
`problems()`'s selection call still never passes `meta`, so the enforcement path itself emits no fallback marker — observability depends on the parallel counting call, not the used result.
NIT: `import logging` inside `_latest_review` runs on every call; module-level import matches the `fix_guard` pattern (extends the prior import-placement NIT).
prefer_sha early-return sets `mtime_fallback=True` when `at` is empty even though mtime did not participate in that selection, conflating "degraded record" with "mtime used".
SUMMARY: Delta resolves the prior unconditional `status=ok` bug and makes closed-skip + mtime fallback explicit on the `--all` path and via architect_review's warning; language rule respected (tooling Python) and the shared-selector/`core/backlog` authority direction matches the approved contract.
Top risks: untested `is_closed` semantics change against the backlog status authority (could flip AC-1 skip behavior) and the redundant per-item double selection used only for fallback counting.

MINOR: `is_closed` now lowercases the status before calling `backlog.section(...)` (review_select.py delta), changing the input casing given to the status authority; mixed-case statuses not present in `CLOSED_STATUSES` (e.g. stored `WONT_FIX`/`Done` variants) may resolve differently than the prior raw-status call.

The new `problems(item, c, meta=meta)` threading in `fix_guard.py` has no regression test; a dropped/reverted `meta` would make `mtime_fallback` print `0` while fallback selection still occurs, weakening AC-3 observability (test added only covers `review_select.is_closed` + `latest_review` meta).

`--item` path still reports no closed-skip marker: a closed item makes `problems()` return `[]` and the tool prints `OK` with no `skipped_closed` equivalent, while the delta touched this path (only `--all` makes skipping explicit).
NIT: `--item` observability line (`fix-guard: item=<id> mtime_fallback=<n>`) uses a different shape than the `--all` line (`status=... skipped_closed=... mtime_fallback=...`), making guard output inconsistent for log scraping.

`test_closed_status_authority_covers_all_closed_values` hardcodes a status vocabulary that must stay in sync with `CLOSED_STATUSES`/`backlog.section`; deriving the open/closed cases from the source of truth would prevent drift.
SUMMARY: Delta resolves the prior pending findings: `is_closed` re-adds an explicit `CLOSED_STATUSES` authority with a covering test, `meta` is threaded once through `problems()` (double `latest_review` call removed), `--item` fallback is now printed, `import logging` is module-level, and the `prefer_sha` early-return no longer mislabels `mtime_fallback`.

No blockers or contract breaks in the delta; residual risks are the casing change to the backlog status authority call, untested `meta` threading, and continued silence of closed-skip on the single-item path.

MINOR: The delta-added `--item` closed-skip branch (`fix_guard.py`: `skipped = 1 if is_closed(...)` / `if not skipped: bad += ...`) has no regression test; a dropped guard would silently re-enforce closed items or lose the `skipped_closed` marker, weakening AC-3 for this path.

The `is_closed` case-boundary change (raw value now passed to `backlog.section`) is untested: no test covers a mixed-case authority-dependent status (e.g. `WONT_FIX` vs `wont_fix`), so the exact contract with the case-sensitivity of `backlog.section` remains implicit (fail-closed direction only).

The new `test_fix_guard_problems_threads_meta` patches `fg.latest_review`, so it only holds if `problems` resolves that symbol at module scope; it verifies meta threading but not that the printed `mtime_fallback=` line reflects it end-to-end.
NIT: When `--item` skips a closed item, `meta` stays empty and the line prints `mtime_fallback=0`, which is indistinguishable from "evaluated, no fallback"; consider an explicit "not evaluated" marker for log scraping.
Output-shape unification in `--item` is good, but the line still omits the item id (`item=<id>`), so `--all` and `--item` records are not uniformly greppable.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly resolves the prior MINORs (raw status to authority, meta threading test, `--item` skip marker, output-shape NIT) and stays within the approved scope with tooling-Python language rule satisfied.
Remaining risks are test-coverage gaps on the new `--item` skip path and the unverified case-sensitivity contract at the `backlog.section` boundary.
No blocker or contract-breaking issue; approve with the MINOR test additions.

MINOR: `review_select.py` delta: `norm.replace("_", "")` is unbounded string mangling instead of an explicit status alias map; `won_tfix`→`wontfix`-style collisions can silently widen the closed set, weakening the "closed status comes from the authoritative backlog" invariant (design contract, `is_closed` hunk).

The new `test_mixed_case_closed_status` passes via the raw-lower branch if `CLOSED_STATUSES` already contains `wont_fix`, so the added `replace("_","")` path may have zero coverage; add a case only reachable through normalization to prove which branch decides closure.

Prior finding disposition=ACTIONED is not fully substantiated: no delta test asserts the printed `mtime_fallback=` line end-to-end with populated `meta` (the new tests cover `skipped_closed`/`item=` and `is_closed` only), so the observability half of AC-3 for the mtime path remains untested.

`test_item_closed_skip_output` stubs `backlog.get_epic`, so it verifies skip plumbing/output shape but not that a real authoritative closed status reaches `is_closed`; combined with the underscore change, the authority→skip wiring is only indirectly covered.
NIT: `test_item_closed_skip_output` asserts loose substrings (`skipped_closed=1`, `item=BI-PF-7`) without pinning `status=ok` on the same line, so a regression that reports skip but still fails the item would pass the test.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly resolves the pending greppability NIT (`item=<id>`) and adds closed-skip/mixed-case tests; no blockers and no AC regression in the delta.

Top risks: the underscore-normalization in `is_closed` is an implicit, possibly untested widening of the closed set, and one prior disposition (printed `mtime_fallback` observability) is marked ACTIONED without covering evidence.
Recommend explicit status aliasing plus one end-to-end assertion of the printed fallback marker before merge.

MINOR: Delta introduces `_J = "." + "json"` and interpolates it into every test filename, an unexplained string indirection that obscures the artifact under test (`.json` review files) and reads as scanner-evasion rather than intent; if a rule required this, cite it in a comment, otherwise use plain literals.

Delta only rewrites test path literals; the prior PENDING NIT (skip-output test does not pin `status=ok` on the same line as `skipped_closed=1`, so a skip-and-still-fail regression passes) remains unaddressed in this change.
SUMMARY: Delta is a test-only literal refactor; AC-1/2/3 evidence and shared-selector behavior are not broken by it, so no blocker or major.
Main concerns: unexplained `.json`-obfuscation harms maintainability, and the one still-PENDING observability assertion from the prior review is untouched by this delta.

mtime fallback is a silent gate-ordering path: a legacy review with no `at` can win selection with zero runtime evidence that degraded ordering was used (test coverage does not make it observable in CI output).

`fix_guard.problems` now returns `[]` before the `fix_impact missing` check whenever the selected review has no BLOCKER/MAJOR findings (or no review is found) — silently drops existing enforcement; behavior change not authorized by the approved contract ("No change to review findings or dispositions").
`status=ok` is printed unconditionally in the `--all` branch before `bad` is evaluated, so a failing gate still emits `status=ok` — misleading observability that undermines AC-3.

`CLOSED_STATUSES` is hardcoded in `review_select.py` instead of reusing the `core/backlog.py` status authority named in design dependencies; vocabulary drift risks wrongly enforcing (or skipping) items as backlog statuses evolve.

`is_closed` now delegates to `backlog.section({"status": ...}) == "done"` (review_select.py delta); equivalence to the prior CLOSED_STATUSES set is unproven and untested — if section() maps only literal "done", previously-closed statuses stop being skipped and get enforced (AC-1 regression); if it maps broadly, open items could be silently skipped (gate bypass).

No delta test exercises the changed `is_closed` authority path or asserts the new fix-guard `mtime_fallback=<n>` output; the only added test covers `review_select.latest_review` meta, so the closed-skip semantics change ships without a fail-able test (design guardrail: no silent behaviour change without a test).
